rect.title: This diagram is drawn from ply.yaml, the file describing this codebase's architecture and verification claims. Each box is a component; chips are functions with their declared checks; arrows are permitted calls (solid) and data flows (dashed); red bars are forbidden calls. A box's grey depth is how strongly it promises to be checked — white means something inside promises nothing, deeper grey means stronger checks promised, and the weakest function sets the whole box's shade. Nothing here is green: green is kept for evidence a run has actually earned, which this render never sees, so a picture full of promises should not look like a picture full of results. Hover anything for its meaning.

g.title: ply.yaml — the document this picture is drawn from. Everything you see here was declared in it; nothing was inferred from code. What each box has actually been checked for is what `cargo ply verify` reports, not this drawing. ply: 1 — the format version every rule below is read under; a version this build does not speak is refused, never guessed at

What this document declares. "1 function promises nothing" counts functions that end up with nothing checked -- whether nobody wrote any checks for them, or the document switched checking off for them on purpose. Running `cargo ply verify` is what turns promises into results; this line never reports results.
`*` stands for every component
no component may call feed — such a call fails the build
`*` stands for every component
no component may call book — except decoder — such a call fails the build

#7 marks an unresolved decision — a question the design still owes an answer: backpressure policy when the ring is full: drop frame vs spin. It belongs to the workspace as a whole, not to any function or component yet; Ply tracks it until someone resolves it (§5.6).

component feed — maps to Rust module ingest::feed capabilities: net promises nothing as a whole — something inside declares no checks, and one unchecked thing sets the level of everything around it (unclaimed) this box is hatched because `Feed::pump` declares no checks at all — one unchecked thing inside sets the shade of everything around it

this component may use `net`. A component may use only the capabilities it declares — that limit is declared here, and not checked by this build: Ply currently compares crate-level dependencies and does not yet look inside functions, so use of a capability this component never declared can still go unnoticed (§5.3)
Feed::pump no checks declared — nothing about this function is verified (unclaimed)

component ring — maps to Rust module disruptor::spsc capabilities: unsafe owns disruptor::spsc::Spsc — only this component may mutate them profile hot_path — a named bundle of extra rules this component must follow: no_panics (functions here must never panic (crash on purpose)), exhaustive_match (every match must handle all cases explicitly) declares checks up to bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — the strongest verdict this could earn if every declared check ran and passed; a promise, never a result this box is this shade because `Spsc::try_push` is the weakest thing in it: it declares bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — nothing here is drawn stronger than its weakest part

this component may use `unsafe`. A component may use only the capabilities it declares — that limit is declared here, and not checked by this build: Ply currently compares crate-level dependencies and does not yet look inside functions, so use of a capability this component never declared can still go unnoticed (§5.3)

profile `hot_path` — a named bundle of extra rules this component must follow: no_panics (functions here must never panic (crash on purpose)), exhaustive_match (every match must handle all cases explicitly)

Spsc::try_push bounded(3) — Kani symbolically checks supported inputs that satisfy requires against ensures; 3 is the maximum loop-unwind depth, not a numeric input limit; collection inputs may also be limited to length 3 generic — every check runs with T=ingest::feed::RawFrame; whatever they earn covers only that type

Spsc::try_pop bounded(3) — Kani symbolically checks supported inputs that satisfy requires against ensures; 3 is the maximum loop-unwind depth, not a numeric input limit; collection inputs may also be limited to length 3 generic — every check runs with T=ingest::feed::RawFrame; whatever they earn covers only that type

component decoder — maps to Rust module ingest::decode pure — the double border is the seal: this component declares no capabilities and may not use any. That is declared here, and not checked by this build: Ply currently compares crate-level dependencies and does not yet look inside functions, so capability use inside this sealed component can still go unnoticed (§5.3) profile hot_path — a named bundle of extra rules this component must follow: no_panics (functions here must never panic (crash on purpose)), exhaustive_match (every match must handle all cases explicitly) declares checks up to bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — the strongest verdict this could earn if every declared check ran and passed; a promise, never a result this box is this shade because `decode` is the weakest thing in it: it declares bounded — proved for every input up to a loop bound — nothing here is drawn stronger than its weakest part

profile `hot_path` — a named bundle of extra rules this component must follow: no_panics (functions here must never panic (crash on purpose)), exhaustive_match (every match must handle all cases explicitly)

decode bounded(2) — Kani symbolically checks supported inputs that satisfy requires against ensures; 2 is the maximum loop-unwind depth, not a numeric input limit; collection inputs may also be limited to length 2 fuzz(4096) — tries 4096 generated inputs that satisfy requires, then checks ensures mutate — plants small deliberate bugs; test/fuzz must catch each one or the requires/ensures are too weak 1 worked example, written down but not run: no check here asks for the declared examples, so nothing compiles them
